questions.subtopic: Goodwill Impairment — Testing Other Assets of the Reporting Unit First
questions.stem: At its annual impairment testing date, Corvallis Corp. tests the goodwill of its outdoor equipment reporting unit. Immediately before any impairment testing, the reporting unit's carrying amount is $18,400,000, which includes goodwill of $3,000,000 and an indefinite-lived trademark with a carrying amount of $2,500,000. The fair value of the trademark is $1,900,000, and the fair value of the reporting unit as a whole is $16,500,000. No other assets of the reporting unit are impaired. Ignoring income taxes, what amount of goodwill impairment loss should Corvallis recognize?
questions.explanation: Assets other than goodwill (including indefinite-lived intangibles) are tested for impairment and adjusted before the goodwill test. The trademark is written down by $600,000 ($2,500,000 − $1,900,000), so the reporting unit's carrying amount becomes $17,800,000. Under the one-step goodwill test, the goodwill impairment is the excess of that carrying amount over the unit's fair value: $17,800,000 − $16,500,000 = $1,300,000, which does not exceed the $3,000,000 of goodwill. The $1,900,000 answer compares the fair value with the carrying amount before the trademark write-down, which double counts the $600,000 trademark loss in goodwill. The $600,000 answer is the trademark impairment, not the goodwill impairment. The $3,000,000 answer writes off all goodwill even though the shortfall is smaller than the goodwill balance.
questions.explanationJa: のれん以外の資産（無期限の無形資産を含む）を先に減損テストし、帳簿価額を修正してから、のれんのテストを行う。商標を$600,000（$2,500,000 − $1,900,000）減額すると、報告単位の帳簿価額は$17,800,000になる。1ステップテストでは、のれんの減損損失は帳簿価額が公正価値を超える額であり、$17,800,000 − $16,500,000 = $1,300,000（のれん残高$3,000,000以内）となる。$1,900,000は商標の減額前の帳簿価額と比較しており、商標の損失$600,000をのれんでも二重に計上している。$600,000は商標の減損額であり、のれんの減損額ではない。$3,000,000は、不足額がのれん残高より小さいのにのれんを全額償却している。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill — Results of the Qualitative Screen by Reporting Unit
questions.stem:
Delmar Inc. has four reporting units with goodwill. For the current year's annual test, Delmar documented the following:
Unit 1 | Qualitative assessment performed; concluded it is not more likely than not that fair value is less than carrying amount
Unit 2 | Delmar elected to bypass the qualitative assessment this year
Unit 3 | Qualitative assessment performed; concluded it is more likely than not that fair value is less than carrying amount
Unit 4 | Delmar bypassed the qualitative assessment last year; this year it performed a qualitative assessment and concluded it is not more likely than not that fair value is less than carrying amount
For which reporting units must Delmar perform the quantitative goodwill impairment test this year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Unit 3 only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Units 1, 2, and 3

choices.label: C
choices.text: Units 2 and 3 only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Units 2, 3, and 4

questions.explanation: An entity may assess qualitative factors first; if it concludes it is not more likely than not that a reporting unit's fair value is less than its carrying amount, no quantitative test is needed (Unit 1). If the qualitative assessment points the other way, the quantitative test is required (Unit 3). An entity may also bypass the qualitative assessment for any unit in any period and go directly to the quantitative test (Unit 2). Bypassing in one period does not prevent the entity from performing the qualitative assessment in a later period, so Unit 4's favorable qualitative conclusion ends the analysis. Requiring the test for Unit 4 wrongly assumes a bypass is a permanent election, and including Unit 1 ignores that a favorable qualitative conclusion is sufficient.
questions.explanationJa: 企業はまず定性的要因を評価することができ、報告単位の公正価値が帳簿価額を下回る可能性が50%超ではないと結論づければ、定量テストは不要である（Unit 1）。定性評価で逆の結論になれば定量テストが必要（Unit 3）。また、どの報告単位でもどの期でも定性評価を省略して直接定量テストを行うことができる（Unit 2）。ある期に省略しても、後の期に定性評価を再開することは妨げられないため、Unit 4は有利な定性評価の結論で終わる。Unit 4を含める答えは省略を恒久的な選択と誤解しており、Unit 1を含める答えは有利な定性評価の結論だけで足りることを無視している。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill — Identifying Reporting Units Within an Operating Segment
questions.stem: Harwood Corp.'s Industrial operating segment consists of three components: Alpha, Beta, and Gamma. Each component is a business, has discrete financial information available, and has its operating results regularly reviewed by the segment manager. Alpha and Beta manufacture similar products, use similar production processes, sell to the same class of customers, and share assets and resources. Gamma provides field maintenance services and has economic characteristics that differ from those of Alpha and Beta. How many reporting units does the Industrial segment contain for goodwill impairment testing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One reporting unit: the Industrial segment as a whole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two reporting units: Alpha and Beta combined, and Gamma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Three reporting units: Alpha, Beta, and Gamma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Two reporting units: Alpha and Beta separately, with Gamma's goodwill assigned to corporate

questions.explanation: A reporting unit is an operating segment or one level below (a component). A component is a reporting unit if it is a business with discrete financial information that segment management regularly reviews. All three components meet that test, but components of the same operating segment with similar economic characteristics must be aggregated into a single reporting unit. Alpha and Beta are therefore combined, while Gamma, with dissimilar economics, remains a separate reporting unit, giving two reporting units. Treating the whole segment as one unit ignores that the components qualify on their own; counting three units ignores the aggregation requirement; and goodwill cannot be parked at corporate when an operating reporting unit benefits from it.
questions.explanationJa: 報告単位とは、事業セグメントまたはその1つ下のレベル（構成単位）である。構成単位が事業であり、個別の財務情報があり、セグメント経営者が定期的に検討していれば報告単位となる。3つとも条件を満たすが、同じ事業セグメント内で経済的特性が類似する構成単位は1つの報告単位に集約しなければならない。したがってAlphaとBetaは統合され、経済的特性が異なるGammaは別の報告単位となり、合計2つとなる。セグメント全体を1単位とする答えは構成単位が単独で要件を満たすことを無視しており、3単位とする答えは集約要件を無視している。また、事業を行う報告単位が便益を受けるのれんを本社に配分することはできない。

questions.subtopic: Internal-Use Software — Year-End Carrying Amount
questions.stem:
Kentmore Corp. developed a payroll system solely for internal use. On March 1, Year 1, management authorized and committed funding for the project, and it was probable that the project would be completed and the software used as intended. Kentmore incurred the following costs in Year 1:
Cost | Amount
Vendor demonstrations and evaluation of alternatives (January–February) | $90,000
Design of the chosen software configuration and interfaces | $240,000
Coding and installation | $520,000
Testing, including parallel processing | $140,000
Conversion of data from the old system | $60,000
Training of employees | $45,000
Allocated general and administrative overhead | $35,000
The software was substantially complete and ready for its intended use on October 1, Year 1. Kentmore amortizes internal-use software on a straight-line basis over five years. What is the carrying amount of the capitalized software at December 31, Year 1?
questions.explanation: Only application development stage costs are capitalized: design of the chosen configuration ($240,000), coding and installation ($520,000), and testing including parallel processing ($140,000), for a total of $900,000. Preliminary project stage costs (evaluation of alternatives), data conversion, training, and general and administrative overhead are expensed. Amortization begins when the software is ready for its intended use: $900,000 ÷ 5 × 3/12 = $45,000, leaving a carrying amount of $855,000. The $900,000 answer omits the October–December amortization. The $940,500 answer capitalizes the $90,000 of preliminary stage costs ($990,000 less $49,500 of amortization). The $954,750 answer capitalizes data conversion and training ($1,005,000 less $50,250 of amortization).
questions.explanationJa: 資本化できるのはアプリケーション開発段階の費用のみで、選定した構成の設計$240,000、コーディングとインストール$520,000、並行処理を含むテスト$140,000の合計$900,000である。予備的プロジェクト段階の費用（代替案の評価）、データ変換、研修、一般管理費の配賦額は費用処理する。償却は意図した用途に使用可能になった時点から開始するため、$900,000 ÷ 5 × 3/12 = $45,000となり、帳簿価額は$855,000である。$900,000は10〜12月の償却を漏らしている。$940,500は予備段階の$90,000を資本化している（$990,000 − 償却$49,500）。$954,750はデータ変換と研修を資本化している（$1,005,000 − 償却$50,250）。

questions.subtopic: Software to Be Sold — Working Model Approach and Year-End Balance
questions.stem:
Zephyr Software develops a logistics application to be sold to customers. Zephyr did not prepare a detail program design; technological feasibility was established when a working model was completed on March 31, Year 1. Costs incurred in Year 1 were as follows:
Cost | Amount
Planning, design, coding, and testing through completion of the working model | $1,150,000
Coding and testing after completion of the working model | $420,000
Producing product masters | $80,000
Duplicating software, documentation, and packaging for units to be sold | $65,000
Customer support after general release | $30,000
The product was released for sale on October 1, Year 1, with an estimated economic life of four years. Year 1 gross revenue from the product was $300,000, and anticipated future gross revenue is $1,700,000. Net realizable value of the product exceeds its carrying amount. What amount should Zephyr report as capitalized software development costs at December 31, Year 1?
questions.explanation: When technological feasibility is established by a working model, all costs incurred up to that point are research and development expense. Costs after feasibility and before general release are capitalized: $420,000 of coding and testing plus $80,000 of product masters, or $500,000. Duplication, documentation, and packaging costs are inventory, and post-release customer support is expensed. Annual amortization is the greater of the revenue ratio and straight-line: the revenue ratio is $300,000 ÷ ($300,000 + $1,700,000) = 15%, or $75,000; straight-line for three of 48 months is $31,250. The greater amount, $75,000, leaves $425,000. The $468,750 answer uses straight-line amortization. The $480,250 answer adds the $65,000 of duplication costs to the asset before amortizing. The $500,000 answer records no amortization.
questions.explanationJa: 技術的実現可能性を作業モデルで確立した場合、それまでに発生した費用はすべて研究開発費である。実現可能性の確立後から一般販売開始までの費用、すなわちコーディング・テスト$420,000と製品マスター作成$80,000の計$500,000を資本化する。複製・マニュアル・梱包費は棚卸資産、販売後のカスタマーサポートは費用である。年間償却額は収益比率法と定額法の大きい方で、収益比率は$300,000 ÷（$300,000 + $1,700,000）= 15%で$75,000、定額法は48か月中3か月で$31,250。大きい方の$75,000を償却し、残高は$425,000となる。$468,750は定額法を使っている。$480,250は複製費$65,000を資産に含めてから償却している。$500,000は償却を計上していない。

questions.subtopic: Cloud Computing Arrangement — Total First-Year Expense With a Renewal Option
questions.stem:
On January 1, Year 1, Halvorsen Co. entered into a hosting arrangement that is a service contract for a cloud-based warehouse management system. The arrangement has a noncancelable term of four years and a one-year renewal option that Halvorsen is reasonably certain to exercise. The annual hosting fee of $120,000 is paid each January 1. Between January and June, Year 1, Halvorsen incurred the following implementation costs:
Cost | Amount
Configuration and integration with existing systems | $318,000
Testing | $60,000
Manual data cleansing and conversion | $40,000
Training of warehouse staff | $25,000
Business process reengineering | $35,000
The system was ready for its intended use on July 1, Year 1. Halvorsen amortizes capitalized implementation costs on a straight-line basis. What total expense should Halvorsen recognize in Year 1 related to this arrangement?
questions.explanation: For a hosting arrangement that is a service contract, implementation costs are capitalized using the internal-use software stage guidance: configuration and integration ($318,000) and testing ($60,000), or $378,000. Data conversion, training, and business process reengineering ($100,000) are expensed. Capitalized costs are amortized over the term of the arrangement, which includes the renewal that is reasonably certain, beginning when the system is ready for use. The term runs through December 31, Year 5, leaving 54 months from July 1, Year 1: $378,000 ÷ 54 × 6 = $42,000. Total Year 1 expense is $120,000 hosting fee + $100,000 expensed implementation costs + $42,000 amortization = $262,000. The $274,000 answer ignores the renewal and amortizes over 42 months ($54,000). The $257,800 answer amortizes over a full 60 months from the ready date ($37,800), extending past the end of the term. The $598,000 answer expenses all implementation costs as incurred.
questions.explanationJa: サービス契約であるホスティング契約では、導入費用は社内利用ソフトウェアの段階別ガイダンスに従って資本化する。構成・統合$318,000とテスト$60,000の計$378,000を資本化し、データ変換・研修・業務プロセス改革の$100,000は費用処理する。資本化額は、行使が合理的に確実な更新期間を含む契約期間にわたり、使用可能となった時点から償却する。契約期間はYear 5の12月31日までで、Year 1の7月1日から54か月残るため、$378,000 ÷ 54 × 6 = $42,000。Year 1の費用合計はホスティング料$120,000 + 費用処理した導入費用$100,000 + 償却$42,000 = $262,000である。$274,000は更新期間を無視して42か月で償却している（$54,000）。$257,800は使用可能日から60か月で償却しており（$37,800）、契約期間の終了を超えている。$598,000は導入費用をすべて発生時に費用処理している。

questions.subtopic: R&D Expense — Asset-Acquired IPR&D and Excluded Activities
questions.stem:
Quillon Therapeutics incurred the following costs during Year 1:
Cost | Amount
Salaries of laboratory staff researching a new compound | $410,000
Depreciation of general-purpose laboratory equipment used on various R&D projects | $60,000
Special equipment purchased for a single project, with no alternative future use | $150,000
In-process R&D acquired in an asset acquisition (not a business), with no alternative future use | $500,000
Engineering follow-through in an early phase of commercial production | $70,000
Legal fees to file a patent on a product developed in prior years | $25,000
Design, construction, and testing of a preproduction prototype | $180,000
What amount should Quillon report as research and development expense for Year 1?
questions.explanation: R&D expense includes laboratory salaries ($410,000), depreciation on general-purpose equipment used in R&D ($60,000), the full cost of special equipment with no alternative future use ($150,000), IPR&D acquired in an asset acquisition with no alternative future use ($500,000), and the preproduction prototype ($180,000), for a total of $1,300,000. Engineering follow-through in commercial production is not R&D, and patent filing fees are capitalized as part of the patent. The $800,000 answer capitalizes the asset-acquisition IPR&D, which is appropriate only for IPR&D acquired in a business combination. The $1,180,000 answer depreciates the single-project equipment instead of expensing it (expensing $30,000 rather than $150,000). The $1,395,000 answer includes the engineering follow-through and patent fees.
questions.explanationJa: 研究開発費に含まれるのは、研究所員の給与$410,000、研究開発に使用する汎用設備の減価償却費$60,000、他に将来の用途がない特定プロジェクト専用設備の全額$150,000、資産取得で取得した他に将来の用途がない仕掛研究開発$500,000、量産前試作品$180,000の合計$1,300,000である。商業生産初期のエンジニアリング・フォロースルーは研究開発ではなく、特許出願費用は特許として資本化する。$800,000は資産取得の仕掛研究開発を資本化しているが、資本化できるのは企業結合で取得した場合のみである。$1,180,000は専用設備を費用処理せず減価償却している（$150,000ではなく$30,000）。$1,395,000はエンジニアリング・フォロースルーと特許費用を含めている。

questions.subtopic: Acquired IPR&D — Impairment While Indefinite-Lived, Then Amortization
questions.stem: On January 2, Year 1, Brenton Medical acquired Solace Devices in a business combination and recognized an in-process research and development (IPR&D) asset with an acquisition-date fair value of $2,400,000. At Brenton's December 31, Year 2 annual impairment test, the fair value of the IPR&D project was $1,900,000. The project was completed on July 1, Year 3, and the resulting technology has an estimated useful life of five years with no residual value. Brenton uses the straight-line method, and no further impairment occurred. What is the carrying amount of the technology asset at December 31, Year 3?
questions.explanation: IPR&D acquired in a business combination is capitalized as an indefinite-lived intangible asset until the project is completed or abandoned, and it is tested for impairment at least annually. The Year 2 test reduces the carrying amount to $1,900,000 (a $500,000 loss). When the project is completed, the asset becomes finite-lived and is amortized from July 1, Year 3: $1,900,000 ÷ 5 × 6/12 = $190,000, leaving $1,710,000. The $2,160,000 answer ignores the impairment and amortizes the original $2,400,000. The $1,900,000 answer continues to treat the completed technology as indefinite-lived. The $1,520,000 answer takes a full year of amortization although the asset was available only from July 1.
questions.explanationJa: 企業結合で取得した仕掛研究開発は、プロジェクトの完了または中止まで無期限の無形資産として資本化し、少なくとも年1回減損テストを行う。Year 2のテストで帳簿価額は$1,900,000に減額される（損失$500,000）。プロジェクト完了により耐用年数を確定できる資産となり、Year 3の7月1日から償却する。$1,900,000 ÷ 5 × 6/12 = $190,000で、残高は$1,710,000となる。$2,160,000は減損を無視して当初の$2,400,000を償却している。$1,900,000は完了後も無期限の資産として扱っている。$1,520,000は7月1日から使用可能になったのに1年分を償却している。

questions.topic: Revenue Recognition with Data Analytics (Area II)
questions.subtopic: Analytics Output — Bill-and-Hold Exceptions at Year End
questions.stem:
Pemberly Industries' revenue analytics routine extracted all December, Year 1 invoices for goods that remained in Pemberly's warehouse at December 31. All four invoices were recorded as Year 1 revenue. The goods are complete, and each customer has accepted the goods and agreed to pay.
Invoice | Amount | Bill-and-hold requested by customer for a substantive reason | Goods separately identified as the customer's | Ready for physical transfer | Pemberly can use or redirect the goods
INV-1 | $240,000 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No
INV-2 | $180,000 | No (Pemberly proposed the arrangement to meet a sales target) | Yes | Yes | No
INV-3 | $310,000 | Yes | No (held in general stock) | Yes | Yes
INV-4 | $150,000 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No
By what amount should Pemberly reduce Year 1 revenue?
questions.explanation: In a bill-and-hold arrangement the customer obtains control only if all criteria are met: the reason for the arrangement is substantive (for example, requested by the customer), the product is separately identified as the customer's, the product is ready for physical transfer, and the entity cannot use the product or direct it to another customer. INV-1 and INV-4 meet every criterion. INV-2 fails because the arrangement was initiated by Pemberly to meet a target, and INV-3 fails because the goods are not separately identified and can be redirected. Revenue must be reduced by $180,000 + $310,000 = $490,000. The $310,000 answer overlooks that a seller-initiated arrangement lacks a substantive reason. The $640,000 answer also reverses INV-4, which qualifies. The $880,000 answer treats all bill-and-hold sales as ineligible for revenue.
questions.explanationJa: 請求済未出荷契約で顧客が支配を獲得するのは、すべての要件を満たす場合に限られる。すなわち、契約の理由が実質的であること（顧客の要請等）、製品が顧客のものとして区分識別されていること、物理的に引渡しの準備ができていること、企業が製品を使用したり他の顧客に振り向けたりできないことである。INV-1とINV-4はすべて満たす。INV-2は売上目標達成のためにPemberlyが持ちかけたもので要件を満たさず、INV-3は区分識別されておらず振り向け可能であるため要件を満たさない。修正額は$180,000 + $310,000 = $490,000。$310,000は売手主導の契約に実質的理由がない点を見落としている。$640,000は要件を満たすINV-4まで取り消している。$880,000は請求済未出荷の売上をすべて収益不可としている。

questions.topic: Revenue Recognition with Data Analytics (Area II)
questions.subtopic: Analytics Output — Return Rate Trend and Refund Liability Correction
questions.stem:
Lyle Outfitters sells products with a 90-day right of return. Product cost is 60% of the selling price, and returned products are resold at full price with no reconditioning cost. Return terms, customers, and product mix were unchanged throughout Year 1. A dashboard shows the following:
Quarter of sale | Gross sales | Returns from that quarter's sales (90-day window)
Q1 | $2,000,000 | $160,000
Q2 | $2,500,000 | $200,000
Q3 | $2,400,000 | $192,000
Q4 | $4,000,000 | n/a (window open at year end)
For Q4 sales, Lyle recorded a refund liability of $120,000 (with a reduction of revenue) and an asset for expected returned products of $72,000 (with a reduction of cost of sales), based on management's 3% estimate. Using the return pattern in the data, what is the effect on Year 1 gross profit of correcting the Q4 estimate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease of $80,000

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease of $200,000

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decrease of $128,000

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decrease of $320,000

questions.explanation: The data show an 8% return rate in each of the first three quarters ($160,000 ÷ $2,000,000; $200,000 ÷ $2,500,000; $192,000 ÷ $2,400,000), with no change in terms, customers, or products, so the 3% estimate for Q4 is an anomaly. The required refund liability is 8% × $4,000,000 = $320,000, an increase of $200,000 that reduces revenue. The asset for products expected to be returned rises to 60% × $320,000 = $192,000, an increase of $120,000 that reduces cost of sales. Gross profit decreases by $200,000 − $120,000 = $80,000. The $200,000 answer ignores the related asset for returned goods. The $128,000 answer computes the full net amount ($320,000 − $192,000) without recognizing that $48,000 net was already recorded. The $320,000 answer records the entire refund liability again and ignores the asset.
questions.explanationJa: データでは最初の3四半期の返品率がいずれも8%（$160,000 ÷ $2,000,000、$200,000 ÷ $2,500,000、$192,000 ÷ $2,400,000）で、条件・顧客・製品構成も変わっていないため、Q4の3%という見積りは異常値である。必要な返金負債は8% × $4,000,000 = $320,000で、$200,000増加し収益を減らす。返品予定の製品に係る資産は60% × $320,000 = $192,000に増え、$120,000増加し売上原価を減らす。売上総利益は$200,000 − $120,000 = $80,000減少する。$200,000は返品資産を無視している。$128,000は正味額全体（$320,000 − $192,000）を計算しており、既に正味$48,000が計上済みである点を考慮していない。$320,000は返金負債全額を再計上し、資産も無視している。

questions.topic: Revenue Recognition with Data Analytics (Area II)
questions.subtopic: Analytics Output — Unaccrued Retrospective Volume Rebate Across Fiscal Years
questions.stem:
Ashcombe Supply has a December 31 year end. Its contract with Torrent Retail provides a retrospective 5% rebate on all purchases made in the contract year (July 1, Year 1 – June 30, Year 2) if Torrent's purchases for the contract year exceed $5,000,000. An analytics report of Torrent's Year 1 purchases shows:
Month | Purchases
July | $500,000
August | $550,000
September | $600,000
October | $600,000
November | $650,000
December | $700,000
Based on firm orders already received, Torrent's January–June, Year 2 purchases are expected to total $2,400,000, and Ashcombe concludes that a significant revenue reversal is not probable if it includes the rebate in its estimate. Ashcombe recorded all Year 1 sales to Torrent at the invoiced amounts with no rebate accrual. What amount of Year 1 revenue should Ashcombe report from sales to Torrent?
questions.explanation: The rebate is variable consideration that must be estimated at each reporting date. Year 1 purchases total $3,600,000, and with the expected $2,400,000 in Year 2 the contract-year total is $6,000,000, exceeding the $5,000,000 threshold. Because the rebate applies retrospectively to all purchases, each sale is expected to yield 95% of its invoiced amount: $3,600,000 × 95% = $3,420,000, with a $180,000 refund liability. The $3,600,000 answer reflects the reported data with no accrual. The $3,550,000 answer applies the 5% only to the $1,000,000 of purchases above the threshold. The $3,300,000 answer charges the rebate on the full $6,000,000 contract year against Year 1 revenue, including purchases that have not yet occurred.
questions.explanationJa: リベートは変動対価であり、各報告日に見積もる。Year 1の購入額は$3,600,000で、Year 2の見込み$2,400,000を加えると契約年度の合計は$6,000,000となり、基準額$5,000,000を超える。リベートは全購入額に遡及適用されるため、各販売で請求額の95%を受け取ると見込まれ、$3,600,000 × 95% = $3,420,000（返金負債$180,000）となる。$3,600,000はデータどおりで引当を計上していない。$3,550,000は基準超過分$1,000,000にだけ5%を適用している。$3,300,000は契約年度全体$6,000,000に対するリベートを、まだ発生していない購入分も含めてYear 1の収益から控除している。

questions.topic: Revenue Recognition with Data Analytics (Area II)
questions.subtopic: Analytics Output — Revenue Equal to Billings for Annual Subscriptions
questions.stem:
A monthly dashboard at Brightwater Analytics shows that recognized revenue exactly equals billings in every month of Year 1. Brightwater sells one-year subscriptions to a hosted service, billed and collected in full at the start of each subscription, and the service is provided evenly over the subscription term. Year 1 subscriptions were:
Contract | Start date | Annual fee billed
C-1 | February 1 | $120,000
C-2 | July 1 | $96,000
C-3 | October 1 | $144,000
C-4 | December 1 | $60,000
Brightwater recorded all billings as revenue. By what amount should Year 1 revenue be reduced?
questions.explanation: A stand-ready subscription service is a performance obligation satisfied over time, so revenue is recognized ratably over each term. Year 1 revenue should be $120,000 × 11/12 + $96,000 × 6/12 + $144,000 × 3/12 + $60,000 × 1/12 = $110,000 + $48,000 + $36,000 + $5,000 = $199,000. Billings of $420,000 were recorded, so revenue must be reduced by $221,000, which becomes the contract liability. The $199,000 answer is the revenue that should be recognized, not the reduction. The $210,000 answer applies a half-year convention to all contracts. The $420,000 answer defers all billings although part of the service has been provided.
questions.explanationJa: サブスクリプション型サービスは一定期間にわたり充足される履行義務であり、各契約期間にわたって按分して収益を認識する。Year 1の収益は$120,000 × 11/12 + $96,000 × 6/12 + $144,000 × 3/12 + $60,000 × 1/12 = $110,000 + $48,000 + $36,000 + $5,000 = $199,000となる。請求額$420,000を収益計上しているため、$221,000を減額し契約負債とする。$199,000は認識すべき収益額であり、減額すべき額ではない。$210,000はすべての契約に半年基準を適用している。$420,000は一部のサービスが提供済みなのに請求額全額を繰り延べている。

questions.topic: Revenue Recognition with Data Analytics (Area II)
questions.subtopic: Step 4 — Allocating a Discount to Fewer Than All Performance Obligations
questions.stem: Morland Co. enters into a contract to sell a router, a switch, and a firewall to a customer for $90,000. Each product is a separate performance obligation. Morland regularly sells each product separately at the following standalone selling prices: router, $30,000; switch, $20,000; firewall, $50,000. Morland also regularly sells the router and switch together as a bundle for $40,000 and regularly sells the firewall alone for $50,000. What amount of the transaction price should Morland allocate to the router?
questions.explanation: The total standalone selling price is $100,000, so the contract contains a $10,000 discount. A discount is allocated entirely to one or more, but not all, performance obligations when observable evidence shows it relates to them. Morland regularly sells the router and switch together for $40,000 (a $10,000 discount from $50,000) and sells the firewall at its standalone price, so the entire discount belongs to the router and switch. It is allocated between them in proportion to their standalone prices: $40,000 × $30,000 ÷ $50,000 = $24,000. The $27,000 answer spreads the discount over all three products ($90,000 × 30%). The $20,000 answer assigns the whole discount to the router alone. The $30,000 answer ignores the discount.
questions.explanationJa: 独立販売価格の合計は$100,000であり、契約には$10,000の値引きが含まれる。値引きが一部の履行義務に関連するという観察可能な証拠がある場合、値引きはすべてではなく一部の履行義務にのみ配分する。Morlandはルーターとスイッチを$40,000でセット販売しており（$50,000から$10,000の値引き）、ファイアウォールは独立販売価格で販売しているため、値引き全額がルーターとスイッチに帰属する。両者の独立販売価格の比で配分すると、$40,000 × $30,000 ÷ $50,000 = $24,000。$27,000は値引きを3製品すべてに配分している（$90,000 × 30%）。$20,000は値引き全額をルーターだけに負担させている。$30,000は値引きを無視している。

questions.topic: Revenue Recognition with Data Analytics (Area II)
questions.subtopic: Step 5 — Uninstalled Materials in a Cost-to-Cost Measure of Progress
questions.stem: Granger Builders contracts to renovate a customer's office building for a fixed price of $10,000,000, a single performance obligation satisfied over time. Granger measures progress using costs incurred relative to total expected costs of $8,000,000. Expected costs include $1,600,000 of specialized elevators purchased from a third-party manufacturer. Granger is not involved in designing or manufacturing the elevators, and the customer obtained control of them when they were delivered to the site in Year 1, well before installation, which will occur in Year 2. Year 1 costs incurred total $3,200,000, including the $1,600,000 for the elevators. What amount of revenue should Granger recognize in Year 1?
questions.explanation: Uninstalled materials that the customer controls before installation, and whose cost is significant relative to total costs but does not depict progress, are excluded from the cost-to-cost measure; revenue for them is recognized at an amount equal to their cost (zero margin). Progress on the rest of the contract is ($3,200,000 − $1,600,000) ÷ ($8,000,000 − $1,600,000) = 25%. Revenue is $1,600,000 for the elevators plus 25% × ($10,000,000 − $1,600,000) = $2,100,000, for a total of $3,700,000. The $4,000,000 answer includes the elevator costs in the measure of progress (40% × $10,000,000), overstating progress. The $2,100,000 answer omits the zero-margin revenue for the elevators. The $2,500,000 answer applies 25% to the full contract price and still omits the elevator revenue.
questions.explanationJa: 据付前に顧客が支配を獲得した未据付の資材で、総コストに占める割合が大きいが進捗を表さないものは、原価比例法の進捗度の計算から除外し、その原価と同額の収益（利益ゼロ）を認識する。残りの部分の進捗度は（$3,200,000 − $1,600,000）÷（$8,000,000 − $1,600,000）= 25%。収益はエレベーター分$1,600,000に、25% ×（$10,000,000 − $1,600,000）= $2,100,000を加えた$3,700,000となる。$4,000,000はエレベーター原価を進捗度に含めており（40% × $10,000,000）、進捗を過大評価している。$2,100,000はエレベーターの利益ゼロの収益を漏らしている。$2,500,000は契約価格全額に25%を掛けたうえ、エレベーター分の収益も漏らしている。

questions.subtopic: Classification — Substantive Terms and Settlement Features
questions.stem:
Fairhaven Corp. has the following share-based payment awards outstanding with employees:
I. Stock options that Fairhaven may settle in cash or shares at its own discretion; Fairhaven has never settled in cash and intends to settle in shares.
II. Stock appreciation rights that will be settled in cash or shares at the employee's election.
III. Restricted stock units for which Fairhaven withholds shares to cover employee tax obligations, not exceeding the maximum statutory tax rates in the employees' jurisdictions.
IV. Stock options that are nominally share-settled, but Fairhaven has a practice of repurchasing the shares for cash at fair value immediately after exercise whenever employees ask it to do so.
Which of these awards should be classified as liabilities?

choices.label: A
choices.text: II only

choices.label: B
choices.text: I and II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: II and IV only

choices.label: D
choices.text: II, III, and IV

questions.explanation: An award is a liability if the entity can be required to transfer cash or other assets. Award II gives the employee the right to demand cash, so it is a liability. Award IV is a liability because the substantive terms, evidenced by a practice of repurchasing shares for cash on request, differ from the written share-settlement terms. Award I is equity because the cash alternative is at Fairhaven's discretion and it has the ability and intent to settle in shares. Award III remains equity because net share settlement for tax withholding does not exceed the maximum statutory rates. Classifying Award I as a liability ignores who controls the settlement choice, and classifying Award III as a liability ignores the statutory withholding exception.
questions.explanationJa: 企業が現金その他の資産の引渡しを要求され得る場合、報酬は負債に分類される。IIは従業員が現金を要求できるため負債である。IVは、要求に応じて株式を現金で買い戻す慣行があり、実質的な条件が書面上の株式決済と異なるため負債である。Iは現金決済の選択権がFairhaven側にあり、株式で決済する能力と意図があるため資本である。IIIは税金源泉徴収のための差引株式決済が法定最高税率を超えないため資本のままである。Iを負債とする答えは決済方法の選択権が誰にあるかを無視しており、IIIを負債とする答えは法定源泉徴収の例外を無視している。

questions.subtopic: Cash-Settled SARs — Graded Vesting With Tranche-by-Tranche Attribution
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Ellison Co. grants 9,000 cash-settled stock appreciation rights (SARs) to employees. One-third of the SARs vest on December 31 of each of Years 1, 2, and 3, subject only to continued service. Ellison has elected to recognize compensation cost for graded-vesting awards on an accelerated (separate-tranche) basis, and no forfeitures are expected. The fair value of each SAR was $5 on the grant date and $6 on December 31, Year 1, for all tranches. What amount of compensation cost should Ellison recognize in Year 1?
questions.explanation: Cash-settled SARs are liabilities remeasured at fair value each reporting date, and under separate-tranche attribution each tranche is treated as its own award. At December 31, Year 1, each tranche of 3,000 SARs at $6 ($18,000) is recognized in proportion to service rendered: the first tranche 100% ($18,000), the second 1/2 ($9,000), and the third 1/3 ($6,000), for a total of $33,000. The $27,500 answer uses the $5 grant-date fair value, which applies only to equity-classified awards. The $18,000 answer recognizes one-third of the total award, which is a straight-line result inconsistent with Ellison's accelerated policy. The $54,000 answer recognizes the entire fair value although two tranches are unvested.
questions.explanationJa: 現金決済型SARは負債であり、各報告日に公正価値で再測定する。トランシェ別に認識する方法では、各トランシェを別個の報酬として扱う。Year 1末に3,000単位×$6 = $18,000の各トランシェを提供済み勤務の割合で認識すると、第1トランシェ100%（$18,000）、第2トランシェ1/2（$9,000）、第3トランシェ1/3（$6,000）で合計$33,000となる。$27,500は付与日の公正価値$5を用いているが、それは資本分類の報酬にのみ適用される。$18,000は報酬全体の3分の1を認識する定額法の結果で、Ellisonの加速法の方針と矛盾する。$54,000は2つのトランシェが未確定なのに公正価値全額を認識している。

questions.subtopic: Modification — Accelerated Vesting for a Terminated Employee (Improbable to Probable)
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Prescott Inc. granted an executive 10,000 equity-classified stock options with a grant-date fair value of $12 per option that cliff-vest after four years of service. Prescott accounts for forfeitures as they occur and recognized $30,000 of compensation cost in each of Years 1 and 2. On January 1, Year 3, Prescott terminated the executive's employment and, as part of the separation, modified the award so that all options vested immediately. Without the modification, the options would have been forfeited upon termination. The fair value of each option on the modification date was $7. What net compensation cost should Prescott recognize in Year 3 for this award?
questions.explanation: Because the original award would have been forfeited on termination, the vesting condition was improbable of being met immediately before the modification. In this type of modification, the cost previously recognized for the original award ($60,000) is reversed, and the fair value of the modified award on the modification date (10,000 × $7 = $70,000) is recognized because it vests immediately. The net Year 3 cost is $70,000 − $60,000 = $10,000. The $60,000 answer simply accelerates the unrecognized grant-date cost of the original award. The $70,000 answer recognizes the modified award without reversing the original cost. The $130,000 answer accelerates the remaining original cost and also adds the modified award's fair value.
questions.explanationJa: 当初の報酬は退職により失効するはずであったため、条件変更の直前には権利確定条件を満たす可能性は低かった。この種の条件変更では、当初の報酬について計上済みの費用$60,000を戻し入れ、即時に権利確定する変更後の報酬の条件変更日の公正価値（10,000 × $7 = $70,000）を認識する。Year 3の純額は$70,000 − $60,000 = $10,000である。$60,000は当初の付与日の未認識費用を前倒し計上しただけである。$70,000は当初の費用を戻し入れずに変更後の報酬を認識している。$130,000は当初の残額を前倒ししたうえ、変更後の公正価値も加算している。

questions.subtopic: Market vs. Performance Conditions — Year 3 Net Effect When Both Targets Are Missed
questions.stem:
On January 1, Year 1, Winslow Corp. granted two equity-classified awards to the same group of employees, each requiring three years of service:
Award X: 6,000 stock options that vest only if Winslow's three-year total shareholder return exceeds a peer index. The grant-date fair value, which reflects the market condition, is $10 per option.
Award Y: 4,000 restricted stock units that vest only if cumulative three-year revenue reaches $500 million. The grant-date fair value is $30 per unit. Achieving the target was assessed as probable at the end of Years 1 and 2.
All employees rendered service through December 31, Year 3. At that date, neither the shareholder return target nor the revenue target was achieved. What is the net effect of these awards on Winslow's Year 3 compensation cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Net compensation cost of $60,000

choices.label: B
choices.text: Net reduction of compensation cost of $60,000

choices.label: C
choices.text: Net reduction of compensation cost of $120,000

choices.label: D
choices.text: Net reduction of compensation cost of $80,000

questions.explanation: For an award with a market condition, cost is recognized as long as the requisite service is rendered, even if the market condition is never met, because the condition is already reflected in grant-date fair value. Award X therefore continues to be expensed: $60,000 ÷ 3 = $20,000 in Year 3. For a performance condition, cost is recognized only if the condition is achieved. Award Y's $120,000 total cost was accrued at $40,000 per year in Years 1 and 2, and the $80,000 is reversed in Year 3. The net effect is $20,000 − $80,000 = a $60,000 reduction. The $120,000 reduction also reverses Award X, treating the market condition like a performance condition. The $60,000 net cost treats Award Y as if the revenue target had been met. The $80,000 reduction reverses Award Y but omits Award X's Year 3 cost.
questions.explanationJa: 市場条件付きの報酬は、条件が公正価値に織り込み済みであるため、必要な勤務が提供されれば市場条件が達成されなくても費用を認識する。したがってXはYear 3も$60,000 ÷ 3 = $20,000を計上する。業績条件付きの報酬は、条件が達成された場合にのみ費用を認識する。Yの総額$120,000はYear 1・2に$40,000ずつ計上済みで、Year 3に$80,000を戻し入れる。純額は$20,000 − $80,000 = $60,000の減少である。$120,000の減少はXまで戻し入れており、市場条件を業績条件と同様に扱っている。$60,000の費用はYの売上目標が達成されたかのように扱っている。$80,000の減少はYを戻し入れているが、XのYear 3の費用を漏らしている。

questions.subtopic: Nonemployee Awards — Grant-Date Measurement and Cost Attribution
questions.stem: On September 1, Year 1, Ardent Biotech granted 5,000 equity-classified stock options to an outside consultant in exchange for regulatory advisory services to be provided evenly over the next 10 months. The options vest when the services are completed. The grant-date fair value of each option was $8, and the fair value on December 31, Year 1 was $11. Under ASC 718 as amended by ASU 2018-07, what compensation cost should Ardent recognize for Year 1?
questions.explanation: Equity-classified awards to nonemployees are measured at the grant-date fair value of the equity instruments, consistent with employee awards, and cost is recognized in the same period and manner as if the entity had paid cash for the services. Total cost is 5,000 × $8 = $40,000, and four of the 10 months of service were received in Year 1, so cost is $40,000 × 4/10 = $16,000. The $22,000 answer remeasures the options to the $11 year-end fair value, which was the pre-ASU 2018-07 approach. The $40,000 answer recognizes the entire cost at grant although most services have not been received. The $0 answer defers recognition until vesting, which would not occur if the services had been paid in cash.
questions.explanationJa: 従業員以外への資本分類の株式報酬は、従業員への報酬と同様に資本性金融商品の付与日の公正価値で測定し、サービスの対価を現金で支払った場合と同じ期間・方法で費用を認識する。総額は5,000 × $8 = $40,000で、10か月のサービスのうち4か月分をYear 1に受けたため、$40,000 × 4/10 = $16,000となる。$22,000は期末の公正価値$11で再測定しており、ASU 2018-07以前の方法である。$40,000は大半のサービスを受けていないのに付与時に全額を認識している。$0は権利確定まで認識を繰り延べているが、現金で支払った場合にはそのような処理にはならない。

questions.subtopic: Compensatory ESPP With a Look-Back — Cost Across Fiscal Years
questions.stem: Kinsley Corp.'s employee stock purchase plan has a six-month offering period from October 1, Year 1 through March 31, Year 2. Employees purchase shares at 85% of the lower of the market price on October 1 or on March 31. Kinsley determined that the plan is compensatory. Employee payroll withholdings are expected to purchase 50,000 shares. Using an option-pricing model that incorporates the look-back feature, Kinsley estimated the grant-date fair value of each purchase right at $8.00. The market price of Kinsley's stock was $36 on October 1 and $40 on December 31, Year 1. What compensation cost should Kinsley recognize for the plan in its year ended December 31, Year 1?
questions.explanation: A plan with a discount greater than 5% and a look-back feature is compensatory. Its cost is measured at grant-date fair value, which must capture the look-back (here $8.00 per purchase right, more than the $5.40 value of the 15% discount alone), and is recognized over the offering period, which is the requisite service period. Total cost is 50,000 × $8.00 = $400,000, and three of six months fall in Year 1: $400,000 × 3/6 = $200,000. The $135,000 answer measures cost as only the 15% discount on the October 1 price (15% × $36 × 50,000 × 3/6), which ignores the value of the look-back. The $400,000 answer recognizes all cost at grant. The $0 answer defers recognition until the purchase date.
questions.explanationJa: 5%を超える割引とルックバック条項がある制度は報酬性がある。費用はルックバックの価値を反映した付与日の公正価値（本問では購入権1単位$8.00。15%の割引だけの価値$5.40を上回る）で測定し、必要勤務期間である募集期間にわたって認識する。総額は50,000 × $8.00 = $400,000で、6か月のうち3か月がYear 1に属するため、$400,000 × 3/6 = $200,000となる。$135,000は10月1日の株価に対する15%の割引分だけで測定しており（15% × $36 × 50,000 × 3/6）、ルックバックの価値を無視している。$400,000は付与時に全額を認識している。$0は購入日まで認識を繰り延べている。

questions.subtopic: Cash Repurchase of Unvested Equity Options
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Hartwell Co. granted 8,000 equity-classified stock options with a grant-date fair value of $10 per option that cliff-vest after four years of service. Hartwell recognized $20,000 of compensation cost in each of Years 1 and 2. On January 1, Year 3, Hartwell repurchased and cancelled all 8,000 unvested options for $11 cash per option. The fair value of each option on that date was $9. No replacement award was granted. What amount of compensation cost should Hartwell recognize in Year 3?
questions.explanation: Repurchasing an award before the requisite service is complete effectively shortens the service period to the service already rendered, so the unrecognized grant-date cost of $80,000 − $40,000 = $40,000 is recognized at the repurchase date. Cash paid in excess of the fair value of the instruments repurchased is additional compensation cost: ($11 − $9) × 8,000 = $16,000. Total Year 3 cost is $56,000; the remaining $72,000 of the payment (8,000 × $9) is charged to equity. The $16,000 answer recognizes only the excess payment and leaves unrecognized cost unaccounted for. The $40,000 answer accelerates the remaining cost but ignores the excess payment. The $88,000 answer expenses the entire cash payment instead of charging the fair value portion to equity.
questions.explanationJa: 必要勤務期間の完了前に報酬を買い戻すと、勤務期間を提供済み期間まで短縮したことになるため、付与日の未認識費用$80,000 − $40,000 = $40,000を買戻日に認識する。買い戻した商品の公正価値を超えて支払った現金は追加の報酬費用であり、（$11 − $9）× 8,000 = $16,000となる。Year 3の費用合計は$56,000で、支払額の残り$72,000（8,000 × $9）は資本から控除する。$16,000は超過支払額だけを認識し、未認識費用を処理していない。$40,000は残額を前倒し計上しているが超過支払額を無視している。$88,000は公正価値部分を資本で処理せず、支払額全額を費用処理している。

questions.subtopic: Acquisition Method — Goodwill With Mixed Consideration and Transaction Costs
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Strickland Corp. acquired 100% of Pryor Inc. Strickland paid $20,000,000 cash, issued 500,000 shares of its $1 par common stock with a fair value of $18 per share, and agreed to pay additional cash if Pryor meets earnings targets; the acquisition-date fair value of this liability-classified contingent consideration is $1,200,000. Strickland paid $600,000 of legal, valuation, and advisory fees and $150,000 of registration and issuance costs for the shares. At the acquisition date, the fair value of Pryor's identifiable assets was $31,000,000 (including a customer relationship intangible of $2,000,000 not recorded by Pryor), and the fair value of its liabilities was $5,500,000. What amount of goodwill should Strickland recognize?
questions.explanation: Consideration transferred is measured at acquisition-date fair value and includes contingent consideration: $20,000,000 + (500,000 × $18) + $1,200,000 = $30,200,000. Identifiable net assets, including the unrecorded customer relationship, are $31,000,000 − $5,500,000 = $25,500,000. Goodwill is $30,200,000 − $25,500,000 = $4,700,000. Acquisition-related costs are expensed, and share issuance costs reduce additional paid-in capital; neither affects goodwill. The $3,500,000 answer omits the contingent consideration. The $5,300,000 answer adds the $600,000 of advisory fees to goodwill. The $5,450,000 answer adds both the advisory fees and the $150,000 of issuance costs.
questions.explanationJa: 移転対価は取得日の公正価値で測定し、条件付対価も含める。$20,000,000 +（500,000 × $18）+ $1,200,000 = $30,200,000。識別可能純資産は、未計上の顧客関係を含めて$31,000,000 − $5,500,000 = $25,500,000。のれんは$30,200,000 − $25,500,000 = $4,700,000である。取得関連費用は費用処理し、株式発行費用は資本剰余金から控除するため、いずれものれんに影響しない。$3,500,000は条件付対価を漏らしている。$5,300,000はアドバイザリー費用$600,000をのれんに加えている。$5,450,000はアドバイザリー費用と発行費用$150,000の両方を加えている。

questions.subtopic: Contingent Consideration — Measurement Period Revision vs. Post-Acquisition Change
questions.stem: On April 1, Year 1, Danforth Corp. acquired Ellery Inc. and provisionally recognized a liability-classified earnout at a fair value of $900,000 and goodwill of $4,200,000. On August 15, Year 1, Danforth learned that Ellery had signed a large customer contract before the acquisition date that was not considered in the provisional valuation; reflecting that contract, the acquisition-date fair value of the earnout was $1,050,000. At December 31, Year 1, the fair value of the earnout increased to $1,400,000 because Ellery's post-acquisition sales exceeded forecasts. No other adjustments occurred. What amounts should Danforth report for goodwill at December 31, Year 1 and for the effect of the earnout on Year 1 earnings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Goodwill $4,700,000; no effect on earnings

choices.label: B
choices.text: Goodwill $4,200,000; loss of $500,000 in earnings

choices.label: C
choices.text: Goodwill $4,350,000; loss of $350,000 in earnings

choices.label: D
choices.text: Goodwill $4,350,000; loss of $350,000 in other comprehensive income

questions.explanation: The August revision reflects new information about facts and circumstances that existed at the acquisition date and occurs within the one-year measurement period, so it is a measurement period adjustment: the earnout increases by $150,000 and goodwill increases to $4,350,000. The later increase from $1,050,000 to $1,400,000 results from post-acquisition performance, so the $350,000 remeasurement of the liability-classified earnout is recognized in earnings. The $4,700,000 answer adds every change to goodwill. The $4,200,000 answer ignores the measurement period and runs the entire $500,000 through earnings. Remeasurement of a liability-classified earnout is not reported in other comprehensive income.
questions.explanationJa: 8月の見直しは取得日時点に存在した事実と状況に関する新たな情報を反映したもので、1年の測定期間内に行われているため、測定期間の修正である。アーンアウトは$150,000増加し、のれんは$4,350,000に増える。その後の$1,050,000から$1,400,000への増加は取得後の業績によるものであり、負債分類のアーンアウトの再測定額$350,000は損益に計上する。$4,700,000はすべての変動をのれんに加えている。$4,200,000は測定期間を無視して$500,000全額を損益に計上している。負債分類のアーンアウトの再測定はその他の包括利益には計上しない。

questions.subtopic: NCI at Fair Value — Year-End Balance With Basis Difference Amortization
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Holcomb Corp. acquired 75% of the outstanding common stock of Tavish Inc. for $6,000,000 cash. The acquisition-date fair value of the noncontrolling interest was $1,900,000, and Holcomb elected to measure the NCI at fair value. Tavish's net assets had a book value of $6,400,000; the fair value of Tavish's equipment exceeded its book value by $800,000 (remaining useful life of eight years, straight-line), and all other identifiable assets and liabilities had fair values equal to book values. During Year 1, Tavish reported net income of $1,200,000 and paid dividends of $400,000. No goodwill impairment occurred. What amount should be reported as noncontrolling interest in Holcomb's consolidated balance sheet at December 31, Year 1?
questions.explanation: The NCI starts at its $1,900,000 acquisition-date fair value. It is allocated 25% of Tavish's income as adjusted for the extra depreciation on the equipment fair value step-up ($800,000 ÷ 8 = $100,000): 25% × ($1,200,000 − $100,000) = $275,000. It is reduced by its 25% share of dividends, $100,000. The year-end balance is $1,900,000 + $275,000 − $100,000 = $2,075,000. The $2,100,000 answer omits the excess depreciation. The $1,975,000 answer starts from a proportionate share of identifiable net assets (25% × $7,200,000 = $1,800,000) even though fair value was elected. The $2,175,000 answer ignores the dividends paid to the noncontrolling shareholders.
questions.explanationJa: 非支配持分は取得日の公正価値$1,900,000から始まる。設備の公正価値評価差額の追加減価償却（$800,000 ÷ 8 = $100,000）を調整したTavishの利益の25%、すなわち25% ×（$1,200,000 − $100,000）= $275,000を配分し、配当の25%である$100,000を減額する。期末残高は$1,900,000 + $275,000 − $100,000 = $2,075,000。$2,100,000は追加減価償却を漏らしている。$1,975,000は公正価値を選択しているのに識別可能純資産の持分相当額（25% × $7,200,000 = $1,800,000）から始めている。$2,175,000は非支配株主への配当を無視している。

questions.subtopic: Bargain Purchase — Gain After the Required Reassessment
questions.stem: Wakefield Corp. acquired 100% of Lorne Co. for $5,400,000 cash and paid $80,000 of acquisition-related legal fees. Wakefield's initial valuation measured Lorne's identifiable net assets at $6,100,000. Because the initial valuation indicated a bargain purchase, Wakefield performed the required reassessment and identified (1) a present obligation from a pending lawsuit against Lorne with an acquisition-date fair value of $250,000 that had not been recognized and (2) a customer list with a fair value of $150,000 that had not been recognized. No other changes resulted from the reassessment. What bargain purchase gain should Wakefield recognize?
questions.explanation: Before recognizing a bargain purchase gain, the acquirer must reassess whether it has correctly identified all assets acquired and liabilities assumed. After the reassessment, identifiable net assets are $6,100,000 − $250,000 + $150,000 = $6,000,000. The gain recognized in earnings is $6,000,000 − $5,400,000 = $600,000. Acquisition-related costs are expensed separately and do not reduce the gain. The $700,000 answer uses the initial valuation. The $450,000 answer records the lawsuit but omits the customer list. The $520,000 answer nets the $80,000 of legal fees against the gain.
questions.explanationJa: 割安購入益を認識する前に、取得企業は取得した資産と引き受けた負債をすべて正しく識別したかを再検討しなければならない。再検討後の識別可能純資産は$6,100,000 − $250,000 + $150,000 = $6,000,000で、損益に計上する利得は$6,000,000 − $5,400,000 = $600,000である。取得関連費用は別途費用処理し、利得から控除しない。$700,000は当初の評価額を使っている。$450,000は訴訟は計上したが顧客リストを漏らしている。$520,000は弁護士費用$80,000を利得と相殺している。

questions.subtopic: Step Acquisition Obtaining 60% Control With NCI at Fair Value
questions.stem: Oakhurst Corp. held a 20% interest in Penrose Inc. accounted for under the equity method, with a carrying amount of $1,300,000. On July 1, Year 2, Oakhurst paid $3,600,000 cash for an additional 40% of Penrose's shares and obtained control. On that date, the fair value of Oakhurst's previously held 20% interest was $1,800,000, the fair value of the 40% noncontrolling interest was $3,400,000, and the fair value of Penrose's identifiable net assets was $8,000,000. Oakhurst measures the NCI at fair value. What should Oakhurst recognize as a result of obtaining control?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No gain; goodwill of $300,000

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gain of $500,000 in net income; goodwill of $1,000,000

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gain of $500,000 in net income; goodwill of $800,000

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gain of $500,000 in other comprehensive income; goodwill of $800,000

questions.explanation: In a business combination achieved in stages, the previously held equity interest is remeasured to acquisition-date fair value, and the resulting $1,800,000 − $1,300,000 = $500,000 gain is recognized in net income. Goodwill equals the consideration transferred ($3,600,000) plus the fair value of the previously held interest ($1,800,000) plus the fair value of the NCI ($3,400,000), less identifiable net assets ($8,000,000): $800,000. The $300,000 answer carries the old interest at its $1,300,000 carrying amount. The $1,000,000 answer values the NCI at the price Oakhurst paid per share ($3,600,000 for 40%) instead of its given fair value, which excludes the control premium. The remeasurement gain is not reported in other comprehensive income.
questions.explanationJa: 段階取得による企業結合では、従来保有していた持分を取得日の公正価値で再測定し、差額$1,800,000 − $1,300,000 = $500,000の利得を当期純利益に計上する。のれんは、移転対価$3,600,000 + 従来保有持分の公正価値$1,800,000 + 非支配持分の公正価値$3,400,000 − 識別可能純資産$8,000,000 = $800,000となる。$300,000は従来の持分を帳簿価額$1,300,000のまま用いている。$1,000,000は非支配持分を、支配プレミアムを含まない所与の公正価値ではなく、Oakhurstが支払った1株当たり価格（40%で$3,600,000）で評価している。再測定益はその他の包括利益には計上しない。

questions.subtopic: VIE — Primary Beneficiary When Kick-Out Rights Require Multiple Parties
questions.stem:
Ridgeway Solar LLC owns and operates a solar generation facility and is a variable interest entity. Its financing and contractual arrangements are as follows:
Party | Interest | Rights
Aster Equity Partners | All equity, $1,000,000 (about 3% of total capital) | Equity holders have no say in operating decisions; all significant decisions are delegated to the manager by contract
Syndicate of eight unrelated banks | Senior loans, $28,000,000 | Protective covenants only
Mesa Asset Management | Subordinated note, $4,000,000, absorbing losses after the equity; market-rate management fee | Directs operations and maintenance and negotiates power purchase agreements; can be removed only by unanimous action of all eight banks
Which party, if any, is the primary beneficiary of Ridgeway Solar?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aster Equity Partners, because it holds all of the equity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mesa Asset Management

choices.label: C
choices.text: The syndicate of banks, because it provides most of the financing

choices.label: D
choices.text: No party; Ridgeway Solar is not consolidated by any variable interest holder

questions.explanation: The primary beneficiary has both (1) the power to direct the activities that most significantly affect the VIE's economic performance and (2) the obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits that could potentially be significant. Mesa directs operations, maintenance, and power purchase agreements, which drive the facility's performance. Kick-out rights do not take that power away unless a single party (including its related parties) can exercise them; removal here requires all eight unrelated banks, so the rights are not substantive. Mesa's $4,000,000 subordinated note absorbs losses that could be significant, so Mesa meets both criteria. Holding the equity does not give Aster power, and the banks have only protective rights. A VIE that has a party meeting both criteria must be consolidated by that party.
questions.explanationJa: 主たる受益者は、（1）VIEの経済的成果に最も重要な影響を与える活動を指図するパワーと、（2）潜在的に重要となり得る損失を負担する義務または便益を受け取る権利の両方を有する者である。Mesaは施設の業績を左右する運営・保守と電力購入契約を指図している。解任権は単一の当事者（関連当事者を含む）が行使できる場合でなければパワーを奪わず、本問では無関係の8行全員の合意が必要なため実質的ではない。Mesaの劣後債$4,000,000は重要となり得る損失を負担するため、Mesaは両要件を満たす。Asterは持分を保有していてもパワーがなく、銀行団には防御的権利しかない。両要件を満たす当事者がいるVIEは、その当事者が連結しなければならない。

questions.subtopic: Partial Sale Without Loss of Control — APIC and AOCI Reallocation
questions.stem: Bexley Corp. owns 90% of Norcott Ltd., a foreign subsidiary. On October 1, Year 4, the carrying amount of Norcott's net assets in Bexley's consolidated financial statements, including goodwill, is $12,000,000, and the noncontrolling interest's carrying amount is $1,200,000. Norcott's cumulative translation adjustment is $500,000, of which $450,000 is included in Bexley's consolidated accumulated other comprehensive income and $50,000 is included in the NCI. On that date, Bexley sells 20% of Norcott's outstanding shares to an unrelated investor for $3,000,000 cash and retains a 70% controlling interest. Ignoring income taxes, by what amount should Bexley's additional paid-in capital increase as a result of the sale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $0; a gain of $600,000 is recognized in consolidated net income

questions.explanation: A decrease in ownership that does not result in loss of control is an equity transaction; no gain or loss is recognized. The NCI is increased by its new share of Norcott's carrying amount: 20% × $12,000,000 = $2,400,000 (from $1,200,000 to $3,600,000). The related portion of the parent's cumulative translation adjustment is reallocated to the NCI: Bexley's share falls from $450,000 to 70% × $500,000 = $350,000, a $100,000 decrease. The entry is debit Cash $3,000,000 and AOCI $100,000; credit NCI $2,400,000 and APIC $700,000. The $600,000 answer omits the AOCI reallocation. The $500,000 answer reallocates AOCI in the wrong direction. Recognizing a $600,000 gain treats the sale as if control were lost.
questions.explanationJa: 支配の喪失を伴わない持分の減少は資本取引であり、損益は認識しない。非支配持分は、Norcottの帳簿価額に対する新たな持分相当額20% × $12,000,000 = $2,400,000だけ増加する（$1,200,000から$3,600,000へ）。親会社の為替換算調整額のうち対応する部分は非支配持分に再配分され、Bexleyの持分は$450,000から70% × $500,000 = $350,000へ$100,000減少する。仕訳は、借方：現金$3,000,000・その他の包括利益累計額$100,000、貸方：非支配持分$2,400,000・資本剰余金$700,000。$600,000はAOCIの再配分を漏らしている。$500,000はAOCIを逆方向に再配分している。$600,000の利得を認識する答えは、支配を喪失したかのように扱っている。

questions.subtopic: Consolidation Eliminations — Consolidated Cost of Sales With Profit in Opening and Closing Inventory
questions.stem: Fulton Corp. sells inventory to its wholly owned subsidiary, Gale Inc., at a markup of 25% on cost, the same markup used in both years. In Year 2, Fulton's sales to Gale were $800,000. Gale's January 1, Year 2 inventory included $150,000 of goods purchased from Fulton in Year 1, all of which Gale sold to outside customers in Year 2. Gale's December 31, Year 2 inventory included $200,000 of goods purchased from Fulton. In their separate Year 2 income statements, Fulton reported cost of goods sold of $3,000,000 and Gale reported cost of goods sold of $1,900,000. What amount should be reported as consolidated cost of goods sold for Year 2?
questions.explanation: Combined cost of goods sold of $4,900,000 is reduced by the $800,000 of intercompany sales. Unrealized profit is computed on the transfer price: with a 25% markup on cost, profit is 25/125 = 20% of the transfer price. Profit in beginning inventory (20% × $150,000 = $30,000) was realized in Year 2 and reduces consolidated cost of goods sold, while profit in ending inventory (20% × $200,000 = $40,000) is deferred and increases it: $4,900,000 − $800,000 − $30,000 + $40,000 = $4,110,000. The $4,100,000 answer ignores both inventory profit adjustments. The $4,112,500 answer applies 25% to the transfer price ($37,500 and $50,000), confusing a markup on cost with a margin on selling price. The $4,910,000 answer fails to eliminate the intercompany sales.
questions.explanationJa: 合算した売上原価$4,900,000から内部売上$800,000を消去する。未実現利益は振替価格を基礎に計算し、原価に25%を上乗せしているため、利益は振替価格の25/125 = 20%である。期首棚卸資産に含まれる利益（20% × $150,000 = $30,000）はYear 2に実現するため連結売上原価を減らし、期末棚卸資産の利益（20% × $200,000 = $40,000）は繰り延べるため売上原価を増やす。$4,900,000 − $800,000 − $30,000 + $40,000 = $4,110,000。$4,100,000は棚卸資産の利益調整を両方とも無視している。$4,112,500は振替価格に25%を掛けており（$37,500と$50,000）、原価への上乗せ率と売価に対する利益率を混同している。$4,910,000は内部売上を消去していない。

questions.subtopic: Acquisition Method — Items Recognized Separately From Goodwill
questions.stem: In applying the acquisition method to its purchase of Corwin Manufacturing, Halsey Corp. evaluates several items at the acquisition date. Which of the following should Halsey recognize separately from goodwill?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The value of Corwin's assembled workforce

choices.label: B
choices.text: Costs Halsey expects to incur to restructure Corwin's operations under a plan Halsey is not yet obligated to carry out

choices.label: C
choices.text: A present obligation arising from a pending product liability lawsuit against Corwin whose acquisition-date fair value can be determined

choices.label: D
choices.text: Potential contracts that Corwin was negotiating with prospective new customers at the acquisition date

questions.explanation: An assumed contingency that is a present obligation arising from past events is recognized at acquisition-date fair value when that fair value can be determined, so the product liability lawsuit is recognized as a liability separately from goodwill. An assembled workforce is not an identifiable intangible asset, so its value is subsumed into goodwill. Restructuring costs the acquirer expects but is not obligated to incur are not liabilities at the acquisition date and are expensed when incurred after the combination. Potential contracts under negotiation are not assets at the acquisition date; any value they have is part of goodwill.
questions.explanationJa: 引き受けた偶発事象のうち、過去の事象から生じた現在の義務であるものは、取得日の公正価値を算定できれば公正価値で認識するため、製造物責任訴訟はのれんとは別に負債として認識する。集合的労働力は識別可能な無形資産ではないため、その価値はのれんに含まれる。取得企業が予定しているが義務を負っていないリストラクチャリング費用は取得日時点の負債ではなく、結合後に発生時に費用処理する。交渉中の潜在的な契約は取得日時点の資産ではなく、その価値はのれんの一部となる。

questions.subtopic: Fair Value Hedge — Inventory Basis Adjustment and Later Gross Profit
questions.stem: On October 1, Year 1, Harlan Metals Co. held 10,000 ounces of gold inventory with a cost of $18,000,000. On that date, the spot price of gold was $2,000 per ounce. To protect the value of the inventory, Harlan sold gold futures contracts and designated them as a fair value hedge of the change in the fair value of the inventory based on the spot price. On December 31, Year 1, the spot price was $1,920 per ounce, and the futures contracts had a cumulative fair value gain of $780,000. Harlan closed out the futures contracts on December 31, Year 1, and discontinued the hedge. On February 10, Year 2, Harlan sold all 10,000 ounces for $1,950 per ounce. What amount of gross profit should Harlan recognize on the sale in Year 2?
questions.explanation: In a fair value hedge, the carrying amount of the hedged item is adjusted for the change in its fair value attributable to the hedged risk, and that adjustment is recognized in earnings together with the change in the hedging instrument. The spot price fell $80 per ounce after designation, so the inventory is written down by $800,000 (10,000 x $80), from $18,000,000 to $17,200,000. The basis adjustment stays in the inventory's cost after the hedge is discontinued and flows into cost of goods sold when the gold is sold. Year 2 gross profit = $19,500,000 (10,000 x $1,950) - $17,200,000 = $2,300,000. (Year 1 earnings were affected by the $780,000 futures gain less the $800,000 inventory adjustment, a net $20,000 charge.) The $2,280,000 amount adjusts the inventory by the $780,000 derivative gain instead of by the $800,000 change in the hedged item's fair value. The $1,500,000 amount ignores the basis adjustment and uses the original $18,000,000 cost. The $300,000 amount marks the inventory to its full December 31 fair value of $19,200,000, but a fair value hedge adjusts cost only for the change in fair value since designation.
questions.explanationJa: 公正価値ヘッジでは、ヘッジ対象の帳簿価額をヘッジ対象リスクに起因する公正価値の変動額だけ修正し、その修正額をヘッジ手段の損益と一緒に損益に計上する。指定後にスポット価格が1オンス当たり$80下落したため、棚卸資産は$800,000（10,000 x $80）減額され、$18,000,000から$17,200,000になる。この簿価調整はヘッジ中止後も棚卸資産の原価に残り、販売時に売上原価へ流れる。Year 2の売上総利益 = $19,500,000（10,000 x $1,950）- $17,200,000 = $2,300,000。（Year 1の損益は先物利益$780,000と棚卸資産の修正$800,000の差で、純額$20,000の費用。）$2,280,000は、ヘッジ対象の公正価値変動$800,000ではなくデリバティブの利益$780,000で棚卸資産を修正している。$1,500,000は簿価調整を無視し、当初原価$18,000,000を使っている。$300,000は棚卸資産を12月31日の公正価値$19,200,000まで全額評価替えしているが、公正価値ヘッジで修正するのは指定日以降の公正価値変動分だけである。

questions.subtopic: Hedge Type Identification — Three Relationships
questions.stem:
Ardmore Corp. entered into the following derivative transactions during Year 1, each of which qualifies for hedge accounting:
I. A pay-fixed, receive-variable interest rate swap designed to lock in the interest payments on its outstanding variable-rate term loan.
II. Short crude oil futures contracts designed to protect the value of crude oil inventory currently held in storage.
III. A euro-denominated borrowing designated as a hedge of Ardmore's investment in a wholly owned subsidiary whose functional currency is the euro.
How should Ardmore classify each hedging relationship?

choices.label: A
choices.text: I: Fair value hedge; II: Cash flow hedge; III: Net investment hedge

choices.label: B
choices.text: I: Cash flow hedge; II: Fair value hedge; III: Net investment hedge

choices.label: C
choices.text: I: Cash flow hedge; II: Cash flow hedge; III: Fair value hedge

choices.label: D
choices.text: I: Fair value hedge; II: Fair value hedge; III: Cash flow hedge

questions.explanation: Relationship I hedges the variability of future interest payments on variable-rate debt; fixing those payments with a pay-fixed swap is a cash flow hedge. Relationship II hedges the exposure of a recognized asset (inventory on hand) to changes in its fair value, so it is a fair value hedge. Relationship III uses a nonderivative financial instrument denominated in the subsidiary's functional currency to offset the foreign currency exposure of the net investment, which is a net investment hedge whose effective results are reported in the cumulative translation adjustment. Classifying the swap as a fair value hedge confuses it with a receive-fixed swap on fixed-rate debt, which hedges fair value. Treating the inventory futures as a cash flow hedge would apply only to a forecasted purchase or sale, not to inventory already held. Treating the euro borrowing as a fair value or cash flow hedge ignores that the hedged item is the net investment in a foreign operation.
questions.explanationJa: Iは変動金利借入の将来の利払いの変動をヘッジしており、固定払いスワップで利払いを固定するのはキャッシュフロー・ヘッジである。IIは認識済み資産（保有中の棚卸資産）の公正価値の変動をヘッジしているので公正価値ヘッジである。IIIは子会社の機能通貨建ての非デリバティブ金融商品で純投資の為替エクスポージャーを相殺するもので、純投資ヘッジとなり、有効部分は為替換算調整勘定（CTA）に計上される。スワップを公正価値ヘッジとするのは、固定金利債務に対する固定受けスワップ（公正価値をヘッジする）と混同している。棚卸資産の先物をキャッシュフロー・ヘッジとするのは予定購入・予定販売の場合であり、すでに保有している在庫には当たらない。ユーロ建て借入を公正価値ヘッジやキャッシュフロー・ヘッジとするのは、ヘッジ対象が在外営業活動体への純投資であることを見落としている。

questions.subtopic: Cash Flow Hedge — AOCI Reclassified Through Depreciation
questions.stem: On October 1, Year 1, Brenton Corp., a U.S. company, determined that it would purchase a production machine from a Swiss supplier for CHF 5,000,000 on January 2, Year 2. The purchase was highly probable but was not a firm commitment. Brenton entered into a forward contract to buy CHF 5,000,000 on January 2, Year 2, and designated it as a cash flow hedge of the foreign currency risk of the forecasted purchase. The hedge was highly effective, and the entire change in the forward contract's fair value was included in the assessment of effectiveness. When the forward contract settled on January 2, Year 2, its cumulative gain was $240,000. Brenton recorded the machine at $5,600,000, placed it in service that day, and depreciates it on the straight-line basis over 10 years with no salvage value. Ignoring income taxes, what amount related to this hedge should remain in accumulated other comprehensive income at December 31, Year 2?
questions.explanation: For a cash flow hedge of a forecasted purchase of a nonfinancial asset, U.S. GAAP keeps the hedging gain in AOCI and reclassifies it into earnings in the same periods in which the acquired asset affects earnings. The machine affects earnings through depreciation over 10 years, so $240,000 / 10 = $24,000 is reclassified in Year 2, reducing the effect of depreciation expense. The balance remaining in AOCI at December 31, Year 2, is $240,000 - $24,000 = $216,000. The $240,000 amount omits the Year 2 reclassification. The $0 amount adds the gain to the machine's cost (a basis adjustment), which IFRS 9 requires but U.S. GAAP does not permit for cash flow hedges. The $24,000 amount is the Year 2 reclassification, not the remaining balance.
questions.explanationJa: 非金融資産の予定購入に対するキャッシュフロー・ヘッジでは、米国基準はヘッジ利益をAOCIに残し、取得した資産が損益に影響する期間と同じ期間に損益へ組み替える。機械は10年間の減価償却を通じて損益に影響するので、Year 2に$240,000 / 10 = $24,000を組み替え、減価償却費の影響を軽減する。12月31日 Year 2のAOCI残高は$240,000 - $24,000 = $216,000。$240,000はYear 2の組替を漏らしている。$0は利益を機械の取得原価に加算（ベーシス調整）しているが、これはIFRS 9の処理であり、米国基準のキャッシュフロー・ヘッジでは認められない。$24,000はYear 2の組替額であり、残高ではない。

questions.subtopic: Hedged Item Eligibility — Business Combination Commitment
questions.stem: Under ASC 815, which of the following CANNOT be designated as the hedged item in a qualifying hedging relationship?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A forecasted intra-entity royalty payment denominated in a foreign currency, hedged for foreign currency risk in a cash flow hedge

choices.label: B
choices.text: A firm commitment to acquire another company in a business combination, hedged in a fair value hedge of changes in the commitment's fair value caused by changes in the acquiree's stock price

choices.label: C
choices.text: A recognized fixed-rate loan receivable, hedged for changes in fair value attributable to the benchmark interest rate

choices.label: D
choices.text: A highly probable forecasted purchase of natural gas, hedged for variability in the total purchase price

questions.explanation: ASC 815 prohibits designating a firm commitment to enter into a business combination, or to acquire or dispose of a subsidiary, a noncontrolling interest, or an equity method investee, as a hedged item; the same prohibition applies to forecasted business combinations in cash flow hedges. (The only exception is a hedge of foreign currency risk.) The other three items are eligible. A forecasted intra-entity transaction denominated in a foreign currency may be hedged for foreign currency risk because the exchange rate exposure affects consolidated earnings. A recognized fixed-rate loan receivable may be hedged for benchmark interest rate risk in a fair value hedge. A highly probable forecasted purchase of a nonfinancial item may be hedged for variability in its total price in a cash flow hedge.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 815は、企業結合を行う確定約定、または子会社・非支配持分・持分法投資先の取得や処分の確定約定をヘッジ対象に指定することを禁止している。キャッシュフロー・ヘッジにおける予定企業結合も同様に禁止される（例外は為替リスクのヘッジのみ）。他の3つは適格である。外貨建ての予定グループ内取引は、為替エクスポージャーが連結損益に影響するため為替リスクのヘッジ対象にできる。認識済みの固定金利貸付金は、公正価値ヘッジでベンチマーク金利リスクのヘッジ対象にできる。発生可能性の高い非金融項目の予定購入は、キャッシュフロー・ヘッジで購入価格全体の変動をヘッジ対象にできる。

questions.subtopic: Fair Value Hedge of Fixed-Rate Debt — Net Earnings Effect with Mismatch
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Corwin Inc. issued $8,000,000 of 5-year, 6% fixed-rate notes payable with interest due each December 31. On the same date, Corwin entered into an interest rate swap to receive a fixed 6% and pay SOFR plus 1% on a notional amount of $8,000,000, and designated the swap as a fair value hedge of the benchmark interest rate risk of the notes. The variable rate is reset each January 1 and settled each December 31; SOFR on January 1, Year 1, was 4.2%. On December 31, Year 1, after the annual settlement, market interest rates had risen. During Year 1, the swap's fair value decreased by $120,000 (the swap is in a liability position), and the fair value of the notes attributable to changes in the benchmark interest rate had decreased by $125,000. What is the net effect of the notes and the swap on Corwin's Year 1 pretax income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $416,000 decrease

choices.label: B
choices.text: $536,000 decrease

choices.label: C
choices.text: $421,000 decrease

choices.label: D
choices.text: $411,000 decrease

questions.explanation: Coupon interest on the notes is $480,000 ($8,000,000 x 6%). Under the swap, Corwin receives $480,000 and pays $416,000 ($8,000,000 x 5.2%), a net receipt of $64,000 that reduces interest expense to $416,000. Because rates rose, the receive-fixed swap lost $120,000 of value during the year, and the notes' carrying amount is reduced by the $125,000 decline in fair value attributable to the benchmark rate, producing a $125,000 gain. Both amounts are presented in interest expense. Net effect = $416,000 + $120,000 - $125,000 = $411,000 decrease. The $416,000 amount assumes the two fair value changes offset exactly and ignores the $5,000 difference. The $536,000 amount records the swap loss but omits the basis adjustment to the hedged notes. The $421,000 amount reverses the signs, treating the swap change as a $125,000 loss and the notes change as a $120,000 gain.
questions.explanationJa: 社債の表面利息は$480,000（$8,000,000 x 6%）。スワップでは$480,000を受け取り$416,000（$8,000,000 x 5.2%）を支払うので純受取$64,000となり、支払利息は$416,000に減る。金利上昇により固定受けスワップは$120,000価値が下がり、社債の帳簿価額はベンチマーク金利に起因する公正価値の減少$125,000だけ減額され、$125,000の利益が生じる。両者とも支払利息の区分に表示する。純影響 = $416,000 + $120,000 - $125,000 = $411,000の減少。$416,000は2つの公正価値変動が完全に相殺されると仮定し、$5,000の差を無視している。$536,000はスワップ損失だけ計上し、ヘッジ対象社債の簿価調整を漏らしている。$421,000は符号を逆にし、スワップの変動を$125,000の損失、社債の変動を$120,000の利益として扱っている。

questions.subtopic: Undesignated Forward Offsetting a Foreign Currency Payable
questions.stem:
On November 1, Year 1, Ostrander Inc., a U.S. company, purchased inventory from a French supplier for EUR 400,000, payable on January 30, Year 2. On the same date, Ostrander entered into a forward contract to buy EUR 400,000 on January 30, Year 2, at a forward rate of $1.12 per euro. Ostrander did not designate the forward contract as a hedge. Exchange rates were:
Date | Spot rate | Forward rate for January 30, Year 2
November 1, Year 1 | $1.10 | $1.12
December 31, Year 1 | $1.13 | $1.135
Ignoring the time value of money, what is the net effect of the payable and the forward contract on Ostrander's Year 1 pretax income?

choices.label: B
choices.text: $6,000 loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: $8,000 loss

questions.explanation: The euro payable is a monetary liability remeasured at the spot rate, so the euro's rise from $1.10 to $1.13 creates a transaction loss of EUR 400,000 x $0.03 = $12,000. The forward contract is a derivative measured at fair value based on the change in the forward rate: EUR 400,000 x ($1.135 - $1.12) = $6,000 gain. Both are recognized in earnings without hedge accounting, so the net effect is a $6,000 loss. The $12,000 loss omits the forward contract gain. The $0 answer assumes the forward contract offsets the payable exactly, but the payable moves with the spot rate while the forward moves with the forward rate. The $8,000 loss values the forward at the spot rate ($1.13 - $1.12 = $0.01, a $4,000 gain) instead of the forward rate.
questions.explanationJa: ユーロ建て買掛金は貨幣性負債として直物レートで再測定されるので、ユーロが$1.10から$1.13に上昇したことによりEUR 400,000 x $0.03 = $12,000の為替差損が生じる。先物為替予約はデリバティブとして先物レートの変動に基づく公正価値で測定され、EUR 400,000 x ($1.135 - $1.12) = $6,000の利益となる。ヘッジ会計を適用しなくても両方とも損益に計上されるため、純影響は$6,000の損失。$12,000の損失は予約の利益を漏らしている。$0は予約が買掛金を完全に相殺すると仮定しているが、買掛金は直物レート、予約は先物レートで動く。$8,000の損失は予約を先物レートではなく直物レートで評価（$1.13 - $1.12 = $0.01で$4,000の利益）している。

questions.subtopic: Embedded Derivative — Commodity-Indexed Principal and Host Measurement
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Prescott Corp. issued a 5-year note payable with a face amount of $10,000,000 for cash of $10,000,000. The note pays a fixed 2% annual coupon, and the principal repayable at maturity is increased or decreased by the percentage change in a published gold price index. Prescott concluded that the gold-indexed principal feature is not clearly and closely related to the debt host, that the hybrid instrument is not remeasured at fair value with changes reported in earnings, and that a separate instrument with the same terms would be a derivative. Prescott did not elect the fair value option. On January 1, Year 1, the fair value of the embedded gold-indexed feature was $600,000. At what amount should Prescott initially measure the host debt, and how should it account for the embedded feature after issuance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Host debt of $10,000,000; the embedded feature is not recognized separately

choices.label: B
choices.text: Host debt of $9,400,000; the embedded feature is remeasured at fair value with changes reported in other comprehensive income

choices.label: C
choices.text: Host debt of $9,400,000; the embedded feature is remeasured at fair value with changes reported in earnings

choices.label: D
choices.text: Host debt of $10,600,000; the embedded feature is remeasured at fair value with changes reported in earnings

questions.explanation: All three bifurcation criteria are met, so the gold-indexed feature is separated from the host and accounted for as a derivative. The embedded derivative is measured first at its fair value of $600,000, and the host debt receives the residual: $10,000,000 - $600,000 = $9,400,000. The $600,000 discount on the host is amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method. Because the embedded derivative is not designated as a hedging instrument, it is remeasured at fair value each reporting date with changes recognized in earnings. Leaving the note at $10,000,000 with no separate derivative is appropriate only when bifurcation is not required or the fair value option is elected. Reporting the derivative's changes in other comprehensive income applies only to the effective portion of a designated cash flow or net investment hedge. A host of $10,600,000 adds the derivative's fair value to the proceeds instead of deducting it.
questions.explanationJa: 分離の3要件をすべて満たすので、金価格連動部分は主契約から分離してデリバティブとして会計処理する。組込デリバティブを先に公正価値$600,000で測定し、主契約の債務には残額$10,000,000 - $600,000 = $9,400,000を配分する。主契約の割引$600,000は実効金利法で支払利息として償却する。組込デリバティブはヘッジ手段に指定されていないので、各報告日に公正価値で再測定し、変動は損益に計上する。社債を$10,000,000のまま別個のデリバティブを認識しないのは、分離が不要な場合か公正価値オプションを選択した場合に限られる。デリバティブの変動をOCIに計上するのは、指定されたキャッシュフロー・ヘッジや純投資ヘッジの有効部分だけである。$10,600,000は、デリバティブの公正価値を払込金額から控除せず加算している。

questions.subtopic: Effectiveness Assessment — Failed Dollar-Offset Test and AOCI
questions.stem:
On January 2, Year 1, Kingsford Co. designated a forward contract as a cash flow hedge of a highly probable forecasted purchase of 200,000 gallons of diesel fuel expected in October, Year 1. Kingsford performs quarterly retrospective assessments using the dollar-offset method and considers the hedge highly effective when the ratio of the cumulative change in the forward contract's fair value to the cumulative change in the fair value of a hypothetical derivative falls between 80% and 125%. Cumulative changes since inception were:
Date | Forward contract | Hypothetical derivative
March 31, Year 1 | $95,000 gain | $100,000 gain
June 30, Year 1 | $156,000 gain | $120,000 gain
Kingsford cannot identify the specific event or change in circumstances that caused the June 30 result, and the forecasted purchase remains probable. Consistent with its hedge documentation, Kingsford discontinues hedge accounting as of the last date on which the effectiveness criterion was met. Ignoring income taxes, what amount related to the hedge should Kingsford report in accumulated other comprehensive income at June 30, Year 1?
questions.explanation: At March 31, the offset ratio is $95,000 / $100,000 = 95%, within the 80% to 125% range, so the hedge is highly effective and the entire $95,000 change in the forward contract is recorded in OCI. At June 30, the ratio is $156,000 / $120,000 = 130%, outside the range, so the relationship no longer qualifies. When the entity cannot identify the event that caused the failure, hedge accounting is discontinued prospectively from the last date on which effectiveness was established, March 31. The $61,000 change in the forward contract during the second quarter is therefore recognized in earnings. Because the forecasted purchase is still probable, the $95,000 already in AOCI stays there until the purchased fuel affects earnings. The $156,000 amount continues hedge accounting despite the failed test. The $120,000 amount caps OCI at the hypothetical derivative's change, a measurement of ineffectiveness that no longer applies and in any case ignores the discontinuation. The $0 amount reclassifies AOCI immediately, which is required only when the forecasted transaction is probable of not occurring.
